(i) The changing position of women through new ideas and values is an example of a social change caused by: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'revolutionary change' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Universal adult franchise brought social change. (2)
items.answer: (i) culture (ii) Change that occurs relatively quickly, often suddenly, as in a political revolution. (iii) It gave every adult a vote and changed the distribution of political power.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) culture (ii) Change that occurs relatively quickly, often suddenly, as in a political revolution. (iii) It gave every adult a vote and changed the distribution of political power.

items.stem:
Statement: Rural social structure has changed after independence.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Land reforms, the Green Revolution and democratic institutions altered the distribution of resources and power.
items.markingKey: (d) Land reforms, the Green Revolution and democratic institutions altered the distribution of resources and power.

Traditional relationships of caste, kinship and landholding are deeply rooted there.
They are numerically strong and own a large share of the land.
Land reforms, the Green Revolution and democratic institutions altered the distribution of resources and power.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about social change and its causes is correct?
items.answer: Political changes such as universal adult franchise changed the distribution of power in society.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: Technologies such as the steam engine transformed economies and social relations. Spencer applied evolutionary ideas to society with 'survival of the fittest'. Change can be evolutionary (slow) or revolutionary (rapid).
options: Herbert Spencer opposed the application of evolution to society.
Political changes such as universal adult franchise changed the distribution of power in society.
Technology has no effect on social structure.
All social change is sudden and revolutionary.

items.stem: What is meant by 'urbanisation' in the context of social order and social change in urban areas?
items.answer: The growth of towns and cities and the increase in the proportion of the population living in them.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: urbanisation correctly explained as the growth of towns and cities and the increase in the proportion of the population living in them.

items.stem:
Statement: Slums grow in Indian cities.

items.answer: Migrants cannot afford formal housing and cities lack enough affordable homes.
items.markingKey: (c) Migrants cannot afford formal housing and cities lack enough affordable homes.

People move to areas where their own community is in a majority for safety.
Migrants cannot afford formal housing and cities lack enough affordable homes.

"The Green Revolution increased production but also widened inequalities in some regions. Dominant castes often control land and local power in villages. Social change in villages has often been slower than in towns."
(i) The concept of 'dominant caste' was developed by: (1)

items.answer: (i) M.N. Srinivas (ii) A settlement that emerged with settled agriculture, with small size and personal social relationships. (iii) Land reforms, the Green Revolution and democratic institutions altered the distribution of resources and power.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about social order and social change in urban areas is correct?
items.answer: Mass transport is essential for the functioning of large cities.
items.markingKey: (d) The others are wrong: Urban space is divided along lines of class, community and caste. Shortage of housing has led to the growth of slums. That is gentrification; ghettoisation is the creation of single-community neighbourhoods.

Ghettoisation means the conversion of poor neighbourhoods into rich ones.
Urban space is shared equally by all groups.
Mass transport is essential for the functioning of large cities.

items.stem: The following statement about social order, authority, law, contestation and crime is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Social order is maintained only by force."
items.answer: It is maintained by consent and values as well as by coercion.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (It is maintained by consent and values as well as by coercion.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Dominant castes often control land and local power in villages. In villages, social structure is based on traditional relationships of caste, kinship and land. The Green Revolution increased production but also widened inequalities in some regions. Village panchayats and elections have created new sources of power in rural society."
(i) Explain the term 'urban area', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Rural social structure has changed after independence. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The census defines any settlement with 500 people as urban." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) In the Indian census, a settlement with a minimum population of 5,000, a density of at least 400 per sq km and at least 75 per cent of male workers in non-agricultural work. (ii) Land reforms, the Green Revolution and democratic institutions altered the distribution of resources and power. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: An urban area needs at least 5,000 people, 400 per sq km density and 75 per cent of male workers in non-farm work.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'law' and 'crime'.
items.answer: Law: a codified, explicit rule laid down by the state that applies to all members of society. Crime: an act that violates an existing law.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 for explaining 'law' (a codified, explicit rule laid down by the state that applies to all members of society.) and 1 for 'crime' (an act that violates an existing law.), with the contrast made clear.
